title: Temperature & randomness
blurb: Why the same question can get different answers.

slides.title: Same question, different answers
body: Ask a chatbot the same thing twice and you’ll often get two different replies.
That’s deliberate. At each step the next token is picked with a little randomness, and one different pick early on can send the rest of the reply somewhere new.

visual.caption: Example replies written for illustration.
visual.question: Suggest a name for my cat.

cards.label: First try
cards.text: How about Pepper? It’s short, friendly and easy to call.

cards.label: Second try
cards.text: You could go with Biscuit — warm, playful and a bit cheeky.

slides.title: The pick is weighted, not a coin toss
body: Remember the scores from the last lesson? The next token is chosen at random, but in proportion to those scores.
High-scoring tokens win most of the time. Low-scoring ones win occasionally. Very unlikely ones almost never do.

visual.caption: Probabilities made up for illustration, continuing “The cat sat on the…”.

slides.title: Temperature sets how adventurous the picks are
body: Temperature is a setting that reshapes those scores before the pick. Low temperature favours the top choices even more, so replies are focused and consistent.
High temperature evens the scores out, so less likely tokens get picked more often. Replies become more varied and creative — and more likely to wander off track.

visual.caption: Example replies written for illustration.
visual.question: Describe the sea in one sentence.

cards.label: Low temperature
cards.text: The sea is a large body of salt water that covers most of the Earth.

cards.label: High temperature
cards.text: The sea hums silver lullabies to restless gulls.

slides.title: Choosing a setting
body: Many chat apps choose the temperature for you. Tools for developers usually let you set it.
Either way, it helps to know what it does — and what it doesn’t.

visual.caption: General guidance — the best setting depends on the model and the task.

items.heading: Lower for precision
items.text: Summaries, data extraction and code benefit from consistent output.

items.heading: Higher for ideas
items.text: Brainstorming and creative writing benefit from variety.

items.heading: Not a truth dial
items.text: Low temperature makes answers more consistent, not more correct.

quiz.question: Why can the same question get different answers?
options: The model learns from each conversation and changes its mind
Each next token is picked with some randomness, weighted by its score
The model forgets the question halfway through
Different answers come from different servers
quiz.explanation: Tokens are sampled from the model’s probabilities, so different picks — especially early ones — lead to different replies.

quiz.question: What happens when you lower the temperature?
options: Replies become more focused and consistent
Replies become more creative and surprising
quiz.explanation: Lower temperature favours the highest-scoring tokens, so output varies less from run to run.

quiz.question: You set the temperature as low as it goes. What does that guarantee?
options: The model will refuse to guess
Nothing about accuracy — answers become more consistent, not more correct
The model will show its sources
quiz.explanation: Temperature controls variety, not truth. A low-temperature answer can be consistently wrong.
